solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old space station approaching a celestial object

indicators.note: one piece coming up to the next means they sit side by side, the station then the a

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station, abandoned in 2001

explanation.surface: A defunct space station drifts towards a star or planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mira is a well-known variable star in the constellation Cetus, so it is a celestial body.

clue.text: Sending up musical traveller on island is out of order

indicators.note: sending up in a down clue means reading the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
a rep is a travelling sales representative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A show-tune-loving traveller on an island is mocked for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending up' reverses EVITA, REP, ON and I together, as it reads upwards in this down entry; it looks like mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is out of order is not working, not functioning.

clue.text: I train tot badly — it's wearing

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of I train tot are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coaching a toddler poorly is exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Attrition is a gradual wearing away, as by friction, so it names the noun sense of wearing.

clue.text: Everyone going by taxi unhappy about foreign gentlemen

indicators.note: everyone travelling by cab puts the cab word alongside the everyone word

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
everyone is all

indicators.note: about signals turning the unhappy word round

parts.note: sore means aggrieved, unhappy

explanation.surface: Everyone takes a cab, grumbling about the overseas gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the sore word; 'going by' looks like passing, but means travelling by.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is the Spanish for a gentleman or knight, so these are gentlemen from abroad.

clue.text: Mischievous act, offering sanctimonious words with wish for peace

parts.note: cant is hypocritical pious talk
RIP, rest in peace, the wish on a gravestone

explanation.surface: A prank presented with pious words and a plea for calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a magic spell or a playful trick, a piece of mischief.

clue.text: Art in mobile home represented a piece of mathematics

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters of art in mobile home are reworked

explanation.surface: Artwork displayed in a caravan depicts some maths.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton's result for expanding a power of a sum is a well-known result in algebra.

clue.text: The French, showing courage and determination, survive

parts.note: la is a French word for the
stout means brave and resolute, as in a stout defence

explanation.surface: The French display grit and stay alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to endure to the end, to hold out and get through.

clue.text: Exam subject covering published course

indicators.note: covering means the subject word wraps around the published word

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: A school subject that covers a published syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is a subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or path taken, a course to follow.

clue.text: Ambassador seen in group in paper

indicators.note: seen in places the ambassador word inside the group word

parts.note: a set is a group
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador spotted in a delegation featured in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of paper is a sheet, as in a sheet of A4.

clue.text: Parts of the world where some might understand self-restraint?

indicators.note: some hearers might take the word as another of similar pronunciation, so it is a matter of how it is heard

parts.note: continence is self-restraint, especially over one's appetites

explanation.surface: A puzzle over which regions of the globe value self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the match is approximate: only some listeners would hear the two words as the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe, Asia and the rest are the major landmasses into which the globe is divided.

clue.text: Rough stuff from invader

definitions.meaning: a coarse plant fibre used for sacking and twine
a member of the Germanic tribe that settled in Kent in the fifth century

explanation.surface: Coarse material left behind by an invading army.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fibre for hessian shares its name with one of the Germanic peoples who invaded Britain.

clue.text: Old coin, restricted, being brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the restricted word is read from the end

parts.note: reined in, restricted

explanation.surface: An antique coin, once limited, is being reintroduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French coin of former times, worth a twelfth of a sou.

clue.text: Being most sullen, fades away in debate

indicators.note: in places the fading word within the debate word

parts.note: a moot is a debate or meeting for discussion
dies, as a sound dies away

explanation.surface: The grumpiest participant loses interest during a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Moody means sulky and gloomy, and this superlative is the sulkiest of all.

clue.text: NHS to charge possibly and cheat?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of NHS to charge can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Would the health service starting to charge be a swindle?
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's free public health service.
explanation.definitionFit: To short-change someone is to give them less than is due, a form of swindling.

clue.text: Soft bundle one used for drying channel

parts.note: a wad is a soft mass or pad
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soft pad of material is used for wiping things dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'drying' as what the wad is for; it describes the channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert watercourse in Arabia or North Africa that is dry except after rain.

clue.text: Estate scheme put in place first off

parts.note: a scheme is a plan

indicators.note: the first letter of the placing word comes off

parts.note: to station is to put in position

explanation.surface: A property development plan is put into place at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' drops the S of STATION, leaving TATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A large estate where crops such as cotton or tea are grown.

clue.text: Are gang turning up with yesteryear's rebel to be countenanced?

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue reads the are and gang words from the bottom

parts.note: a lot is a group of people, as in that lot
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rebellious youth of the 1950s

explanation.surface: Should a gang showing up with a 1950s rebel be put up with?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses ARE and LOT into TOLERA. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To countenance something is to allow or put up with it, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: St Paul's fellow possibly troubling me, 'non-saint'

indicators.note: troubling stirs up the letters of me and non-saint

explanation.surface: A cathedral clergyman is bothered by someone calling themself no saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul is not the cathedral or apostle but the capital city of the US state Minnesota.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul is the state capital, so its residents are examples of people from that Midwestern state.

clue.text: Short puzzle engaging African party in quiet room?

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the cut puzzle word wraps the party
short means the puzzle word loses its last letter

parts.note: to stump is to puzzle or baffle
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: A brief crossword absorbs an African political party in a quiet retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' looks like a noun, a crossword, but is the verb meaning to baffle; 'Short' docks its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private room where one is not disturbed, as in an inner sanctum.

clue.text: Quality of the present head, keeping personal

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the head word contains the personal word

parts.note: a ness is a headland
own means personal, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: A boss holding on to private matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being current, of existing in the here and now, as a noun formed from now.

clue.text: Face falling off glass instrument

indicators.note: the face of the glass word, its front letter, drops away

parts.note: a flute is a tall narrow glass, as for champagne

explanation.surface: A glass loses its front and falls to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face falling off' removes the F of FLUTE; the flute is a glass here, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked stringed instrument with a pear-shaped body, played in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Characters getting on in South Africa protected by foreign father

indicators.note: protected by puts the result inside the father word

parts.note: pere is French for father

indicators.note: in sets the on word within South Africa

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Characters getting along in South Africa are shielded by a foreign father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' looks like a phrase about harmony; only 'on' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Personae are the characters in a play or story, as in dramatis personae.

clue.text: Work chewed by dog? Such may be children's book

indicators.note: chewed by means held in the dog's mouth, so the work goes inside the dog word

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A puppy has gnawed some work, perhaps a picture book.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up book has paper figures that stand up when a page opens, a children's favourite.

clue.text: Game with nobody short of energy to go into extra time?

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the energy letter leaves the nobody word

parts.note: none means nobody
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired match with nobody left to play heads into extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: To run on is to continue beyond the expected end, like a match overrunning.

clue.text: Disagreement about your being up to the job?

indicators.note: about turns the disagreement word round

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An argument over whether you are capable of doing the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROW to WOR; THY is the archaic 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worthy of a task means deserving it and good enough for it, an idiom for competence.

clue.text: Money Irishman once used for a flutter?

definitions.meaning: the pound of the Irish Republic before the euro

explanation.surface: An Irishman's old currency spent on a small bet.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a modest bet; to punt is also to gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish pound was called this until 2002, and in British slang the word also means a wager.

clue.text: Oily substance from strange tree put in end of garden

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of tree and put in are jumbled
end of picks the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: An oily liquid comes from an odd tree planted at the far end of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives N, the last letter of garden, which joins TREE and PUT IN before 'strange' mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile oil distilled from pine resin, used as a paint thinner.

clue.text: Criticise books this writer's penned — they are laughable affairs!

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the writer's word goes inside the books word

parts.note: tomes are large books
the writer of the clue is I, so this writer's gives I'm, I am

explanation.surface: A writer slates books they have written as ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing but means enclosed; 'this writer' is the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridiculous situations or farces are called this, from the Christmas stage shows full of slapstick.

clue.text: Judge wants old-fashioned award returned

indicators.note: returned says the award word goes back to front

parts.note: meed is an archaic word for a reward

explanation.surface: A judge wants an outdated prize handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to consider or judge something to be so.
